1. e4 {[from the parent game] The king's pawn, two moves.} e5 {[from the parent game] The same.}
2. Bc4 {[from the parent game] The king's bishop, at his queen's bishop's fourth square. (a)}
Bc5 {[from the parent game] The same. (b)} 3. c3 {The queen's bishop's pawn, one move.} Nc6 {The
queen's knight, at his bishop's third square. (a) NOTE: He plays this knight, to hinder you from
pushing your queen's pawn two moves. If, instead of this knight, he had played his queen's
bishop's pawn one move, your next move might equally take place.} 4. d4 {The queen's pawn, two
moves.} exd4 {The king's pawn takes the pawn. (b) NOTE: He could have prevented this move, by
removing the bishop to his queen's knight's third square. This will make a supplement to this
back-game.} 5. Bxf7+ {The king's bishop takes the king's bishop's pawn.} Kxf7 {The king takes
the bishop. (c) NOTE: If he does not take your bishop, you must take his king's knight, and push
your queen's knight's pawn two steps, attacking his bishop; and afterwards push upon his queen's
knight, in order to retake the pawn with your queen's bishop's pawn. SUPPLEMENT} 6. Qh5+ {The
queen, at the adverse king's rook's fourth square.} g6 {The king's knight's pawn, one move.} 7.
Qxc5 {The queen takes the king's bishop, and will have a very good game.} *
